summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of chronic pancreatitis, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and multiple abdominal surgeries was admitted for acute on chronic abdominal pain. The pain was consistent with a flare of chronic pancreatitis, without evidence of obstruction on CT imaging. He was managed supportively with NPO status, IV fluids, and IV pain control, then advanced to a regular diet as symptoms improved. His blood sugars were low due to poor oral intake, prompting temporary discontinuation of insulin and metformin. Pain and mood improved during the stay. He was discharged home with oral pain medication, Miralax, continued pancreatic enzymes, and instructions to restart diabetes medications when eating normally and blood sugars exceed 130, along with follow-up in outpatient care.
